title: Forecastable Model Adoption Signals — signal definitions, scoring, and probe plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a repeatable, measurable signal set that forecasts which open models (and their quantized/variant flavors) will be adopted by Redwood customers in the next 3–9 months. The deliverable will be: 1) a taxonomy of signals (supply, performance, economics, ecosystem), 2) a scoring rubric that outputs a numeric adoption-propensity score per model-variant, and 3) a probe plan (data sources, telemetry, field interviews, and initial dashboards) to validate the rubric against historical adoption events.

Why this matters: procurement, Dedicated capacity planning, and the Watchtower model-sentinel need forward-looking indicators so Sales and Infra can proactively negotiate capacity or onboard fallback variants. Current reactive workflows cause latency arbitrage and missed reserved capacity opportunities.

Scope / non-goals: includes open-source and major commercial open-model forks we track. Does NOT include custom customer-owned models or narrow vertical proprietary models for this phase. Does not build final ML classifier — this ticket is for signal definition, initial scoring, and validation probes.

Signal buckets (initial draft):
- Supply signals: release cadence, packaging artifacts (GGML / float16 / PTQ), maintainer activity, quantization availability, multi-arch builds.
- Performance signals: published throughput/latency, community microbenchmarks, Redwood-verified small-context microbench runs.
- Economics signals: cloud availability (popular AMIs), spot vs reserved GPU affinity, token pricing announcements or proxies, quantization-related cost deltas.
- Ecosystem signals: third-party tool integrations (RAG providers, vector DB connectors), community adoption (GitHub stars, Docker pulls), pretrained prompt-tuning recipes.
- Procurement/enterprise signals: vendor licensing changes, enterprise SLAs, regulatory region availability.

Scoring rubric (MVP): numeric score 0–100 composed of weighted sub-scores by bucket. Provisional weights: Supply 25, Performance 30, Economics 20, Ecosystem 15, Procurement 10. We will tune weights during validation. The rubric must be explainable in the Console and exportable as CSV for downstream teams.

Deliverables:
- CSV spec of signals + collection method and owner (internal telemetry / external crawl / manual field entry).
- Prototype scoring script (Python notebook) and a reproducible example for 8 candidate models.
- Dashboard wireframe (Console) with trend lines and a model adoption propensity tag.
- Probe plan: list of 10 enterprise customers + hypotheses to validate (e.g., "customers with >X qps and latency SLO Z prefer model variant Y") and a timeline for outreach.

Success criteria (end of cycle):
- We can reproduce scores for 8 models and correlate historical score changes with 2 known adoption events (retrospective validation).
- Acceptable signal coverage: at least 70% of buckets have at least one automated source for top-20 models.
- PM/Revenue/Field sign-off on probe hypotheses and outreach plan.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Heavy manual instrumentation may be required for procurement signals; prefer pragmatic proxies (e.g., vendor job postings or public pricing pages) and mark data as lower confidence.
- Early scores will have noise; we accept exploratory thresholds and will instrument calibration later.

Links / references: PRD draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-prd-forecastable-signals (internal), initial notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-signals/notebooks/forecast-probe (PR: #7423), related Linear: PM-27139 (model-channel-fit heatmap) for mapping to procurement channels.
